tasks.subject: Task 1: The MCP server methods in the backend
tasks.description:
**Goal:** `src/headless/backend.ts` lists, adds, turns on or off, removes and signs in to MCP servers exactly as Electron's `mcp-*` channels do.

**Files:**

- Create: `src/headless/terminal.ts`
- Modify: `src/headless/backend.ts`, `src/headless/server.ts`
- Test: `tests/unit/headless-backend.test.ts`, `tests/unit/headless-parity.test.ts`

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- [ ] `mcp-list` returns `{ file, servers }` with `envNames` and `headerNames` only, never values. `file` is `settings.json` in `muse.configDir()`.
- [ ] `mcp-add`, `mcp-enabled` and `mcp-remove` change only their entry in `settings.json`, keep every other key, and write `enabled: false` to turn a server off (CLAUDE.md invariant 3).
- [ ] `mcp-login` refuses a stdio server with "Only remote MCP servers use sign-in." For an http server it opens Terminal with `cd '<home>' && '<cli>' 'mcp' 'login' '<name>'`, and with `logout` when the second argument is `true`.
- [ ] An invalid name gives the backend's error and writes nothing.
- [ ] The parity test moves the five methods from `notYet` and counts 34 headless methods.

**Verify:** `npx vitest run tests/unit/headless-backend.test.ts tests/unit/headless-parity.test.ts && npm run typecheck` → all pass.

tasks.subject: Task 2: The bridges in the backend, with the token from `start`
tasks.description:
**Goal:** The backend runs the folder bridge and the MCP bridge as Electron's `syncBridges` does, with mMac's own bridge folder and a token that mMac sends in `start` and gets back from `bridge-token`.

**Files:**

- Create: `src/headless/bridges.ts`
- Modify: `src/headless/backend.ts`, `src/headless/server.ts`, `scripts/verify-headless.ts`
- Test: `tests/unit/headless-bridges.test.ts` (new), `tests/unit/headless-backend.test.ts`, `tests/unit/headless-parity.test.ts`

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- [ ] `start` accepts `{ dataFolder, bridgeToken? }`. The token is a string of at most 256 characters and is kept in memory only. It never goes into `preferences.json`, an event or a log line.
- [ ] After `start` connects, the bridges match the preferences. Saving a `bridge*` preference syncs them again, in one serialized chain.
- [ ] The bridge folder is `<dataFolder>/bridge`.
- [ ] `bridge-status` returns Electron's `BridgeStatus`: `folder`, `files {enabled, running, error?}`, `mcp {enabled, running, url, hasToken, error?}`, `activeJobs`.
- [ ] A port in use reports "Port N is in use. Choose another port." as `mcp.error`.
- [ ] `bridge-token` makes a new `randomBytes(24)` base64url token, restarts a running MCP bridge with it, and returns it.
- [ ] The quit path stops both bridges before it exits.
- [ ] An agent request for a project that is not trusted fails with "That project is not trusted in mMac. Open it there first."
- [ ] With the real `McpBridge` on a free port: no token gives HTTP 401; the token gives a reply.
- [ ] `npm run test:headless` also checks that `start` with a token and `bridge-status` work against the real CLI, and that no bridge port stays open after shutdown.
- [ ] The parity test moves `bridge-status` and `bridge-token` from `notYet` and counts 36 headless methods.

**Verify:** `npx vitest run tests/unit/headless-bridges.test.ts tests/unit/headless-backend.test.ts tests/unit/headless-parity.test.ts && npm run typecheck && MUSE_BIN="$(command -v muse)" npm run test:headless` → all pass.

tasks.subject: Task 3: Close the M2 backend gaps
tasks.description:
**Goal:** The backend tests prove what they claim, the login-environment stub is covered and leaves out `MMAC_LOGIN_SHELL`, and **Revert hunk** refuses a hunk that changed.

**Files:**

- Create: `src/headless/login-env.ts`
- Modify: `src/headless/server.ts`, `src/headless/login-env.sh`, `src/headless/backend.ts`
- Test: `tests/unit/headless-backend.test.ts`, `tests/unit/headless-login-env.test.ts`

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- [ ] The `-1` hunk test asserts the zod message (for example `toThrow(/hunk|index|greater/i)` matched to the real text), so it proves the guard runs before `revertHunk`.
- [ ] `createBackendWithAskThatQuits` is gone; the test uses `harness` with an `ask` that sets quitting.
- [ ] The serialized-saves test reads the preferences path from the harness (`h.preferencesFile`), not a hard-coded join.
- [ ] `loginEnvShell()` returns the stub's absolute path and throws "mMac's backend is missing src/headless/login-env.sh." when the file is missing or not executable. `server.ts` uses it. A test checks the real stub.
- [ ] The environment the stub prints has no `MMAC_LOGIN_SHELL`, and a test proves it through `discoverCli`.
- [ ] `git-revert-hunk` takes an optional fourth argument, the hunk text. When it differs from the current hunk at that index, the call fails with "The file changed since this diff was read. Refresh the diff, then try again." and the file is unchanged.

**Verify:** `npx vitest run tests/unit/headless-backend.test.ts tests/unit/headless-login-env.test.ts && npm run typecheck && MUSE_BIN="$(command -v muse)" npm run test:headless` → all pass.

tasks.subject: Task 4: Swift models and typed calls for M3
tasks.description:
**Goal:** `MuseBackend` decodes every preference field and the Settings shapes, encodes their patches, and calls the seven methods. It also closes the M2 transport items.

**Files:**

- Modify: `mac/Packages/MuseBackend/Sources/MuseBackend/Models.swift`, `Methods.swift`, `Transport.swift`, `Launcher.swift`
- Test: `mac/Packages/MuseBackend/Tests/MuseBackendTests/ModelsTests.swift`, `BackendClientTests.swift`, `ProcessTransportTests.swift`

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- [ ] `Preferences` decodes `theme`, `fontSize`, `reduceMotion`, `notifyOnCompletion`, `bridgeFilesEnabled`, `bridgeMcpEnabled` and `bridgeMcpPort`, with Electron's defaults when a field is absent (`muse`, `comfortable`, false, false, false, false, 7735).
- [ ] `PreferencesPatch` sends only the fields set, for the same seven fields plus `cliPath` and `reasoningEffort`.
- [ ] `McpServer`, `McpServerList` and `BridgeStatus` decode Electron's JSON. `McpServerInput` encodes the stdio and http shapes `mcpServerSchema` reads.
- [ ] `start(dataFolder:bridgeToken:)` sends the token only when it is not empty.
- [ ] `mcpList()`, `mcpAdd(_:)`, `mcpSetEnabled(_:_:)`, `mcpRemove(_:)`, `mcpLogin(_:logout:)`, `bridgeStatus()`, `bridgeNewToken()` call the method names of Tasks 1 and 2.
- [ ] `gitRevertHunk(project:path:index:expected:)` sends the hunk text as the fourth argument.
- [ ] `SessionView.usage` is a `var`. `ModelsTests` checks a merge result's `output`.
- [ ] `F_SETNOSIGPIPE` is set only on mMac's own pipe to the backend, not on fd 2. `recentErrorOutput` is gone, and its tests use `errorOutput(waitingUpTo:)`. The deadline comment in `Launcher.swift` is one block.

tasks.subject: Task 5: Settings rules: forms, ports, themes, text sizes and the completion notice
tasks.description:
**Goal:** Pure, tested rules in `MuseKit` for everything the Settings panes decide.

**Files:**

- Create: `mac/Packages/MuseKit/Sources/MuseKit/SettingsRules.swift`
- Test: `mac/Packages/MuseKit/Tests/MuseKitTests/SettingsRulesTests.swift` (new)

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- [ ] `SettingsRules.pairs(_:separator:)` follows Electron's `parsePairs`: blank lines skipped, each line trimmed, the first separator splits, key and value trimmed, a line with no separator or with it first throws "Write each line as name=value: <line>" (or `name:value`).
- [ ] `McpForm.input()` builds a stdio input (command trimmed, one argument per non-blank line, env pairs) or an http input (URL trimmed, header pairs). The name is trimmed.
- [ ] `SettingsRules.port(_:)` returns the port for an integer from 1024 to 65535, else nil. `SettingsRules.portError` is "Use a port between 1024 and 65535."
- [ ] `ThemeName(preference:)` maps `moonlight` and `system` to Moonlight and every other value to Muse. Each has Electron's label and hint ("Electric blue", "Soft and dark").
- [ ] `ThemeName.palette` holds `tokens.css`'s hex values for both themes, as listed in this task.
- [ ] `TextSize(preference:)` maps to compact 14, comfortable 15 (also the fallback), large 17 points.
- [ ] `CompletionNotice.shouldPost(previous:next:enabled:focused:)` is true only for running to idle, enabled, not focused. `CompletionNotice.content(for:)` gives "Muse is ready for you" and the session's name, else its title, else "Your conversation has an update."

tasks.subject: Task 6: The bridge token store and the Settings store
tasks.description:
**Goal:** `MuseKit` keeps the bridge token in the login Keychain behind a small protocol, and a `SettingsModel` store runs the MCP and Bridges panes against the backend.

**Files:**

- Create: `mac/Packages/MuseKit/Sources/MuseKit/BridgeTokenStore.swift`, `mac/Packages/MuseKit/Sources/MuseKit/SettingsModel.swift`
- Modify: `mac/Packages/MuseKit/Sources/MuseKit/Workspace+Actions.swift` (`save(_:)`)
- Test: `mac/Packages/MuseKit/Tests/MuseKitTests/SettingsModelTests.swift`, `BridgeTokenStoreTests.swift` (new)

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- [ ] `BridgeTokenStore` has `read() throws -> String?` and `write(_:) throws`. `KeychainTokenStore(service:account:)` uses a generic password item in the login Keychain. `MemoryTokenStore` keeps it in memory for tests.
- [ ] `KeychainTokenStore.app` uses service `com.domalhambra.mmac.bridge-token`, account `mcp-bridge`. Debug builds take `MMAC_KEYCHAIN_SERVICE` instead when it is set.
- [ ] A Keychain round-trip test uses a random service name and deletes its item, even when it fails.
- [ ] `Workspace.save(_ patch:)` sends a `PreferencesPatch`, sets `preferences` from the reply, and shows a failure in `errorMessage`.
- [ ] `SettingsModel` loads the MCP list; adds a server from `McpForm` (keeping the form on failure and clearing it on success); turns servers on and off; removes one; and signs in. Each change sets `needsReconnect`, which `reconnect()` clears after `Workspace.reconnect()`.
- [ ] `SettingsModel` reads the bridge status on `refreshBridge()` and after each bridge preference it saves.
- [ ] `makeToken()` calls `bridge-token`, writes the token to the store, and shows it once in `newToken`. When the Keychain write fails, it shows "mMac could not save the token in the Keychain: <reason>" and still shows the token.
- [ ] `copyToken()` reads the store and throws "Make a token first." when it is empty.
- [ ] `savePort(_:)` saves a valid port and, for an invalid one, shows `SettingsRules.portError` and returns the saved port as text, so the field resets.
- [ ] An error from any call shows in `errorMessage`, and a stale MCP list read that finishes after a newer one is dropped.

**Verify:** `cd mac/Packages/MuseKit && swift test --scratch-path ../../../.cache/swift-kit --filter "SettingsModel|BridgeTokenStore"` → all pass.

tasks.subject: Task 7: Workspace: turn-finished hook and the carried Workspace items
tasks.description:
**Goal:** The `Workspace` reports each turn that ends, offers the worktree toggle only in a repository, reads Git status once per turn end, and holds itself weakly in badge tasks. The M2 comment and test items close.

**Files:**

- Modify: `mac/Packages/MuseKit/Sources/MuseKit/Workspace.swift`, `Workspace+Actions.swift`
- Test: `mac/Packages/MuseKit/Tests/MuseKitTests/WorkspaceTests.swift`, `WorkspaceActionsTests.swift`, `WorkspaceInspectorTests.swift`

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- [ ] `Workspace.turnFinished: (@MainActor (Session, _ previous: String?) -> Void)?` is called for every `session` event, with the status that conversation had before it, so the app applies `CompletionNotice.shouldPost`. The Workspace keeps the last status per conversation, for every conversation the events name, not only the open one.

- [ ] Every `Task` that reads badges holds the Workspace weakly.

tasks.subject: Task 8: The carried MuseKit rules: diffs, activity titles, Markdown and footnotes
tasks.description:
**Goal:** The M2 items in `InspectorRules.swift`, `Inspector.swift`, `MarkdownBlock.swift` and `Footnotes.swift` close, each with a test.

**Files:**

- Modify: `mac/Packages/MuseKit/Sources/MuseKit/InspectorRules.swift`, `Inspector.swift`, `MarkdownBlock.swift`, `Footnotes.swift`, `TranscriptEntry.swift`; `mac/mMac/InspectorView.swift`, `mac/mMac/MarkdownView.swift` (callers only)
- Test: `InspectorRulesTests.swift`, `InspectorTests.swift`, `MarkdownBlockTests.swift`, `TranscriptEntryTests.swift`

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- [ ] `DiffLine.rawHunks(_ raw: String) -> [String]` returns exactly what `splitHunks` in `src/main/git.ts` returns as `hunks`. A test uses a two-hunk diff with a trailing newline and one with `\ No newline at end of file`.
- [ ] `Inspector.revertHunk` sends the hunk text from the raw diff it read (`git-raw-diff`) as `expected`. If the Inspector parses another diff text, it also reads `git-raw-diff` when the diff loads. On the backend's "The file changed…" error, it reloads the diff and shows the error.
- [ ] A diff line longer than `DiffLine.longLine` (2,000 characters) shows cut, ending in "…". Copy hunk and Copy diff still copy the full text.
- [ ] `ChangeLabel.counted(_:_:)` lives in `MuseKit` with a test; `InspectorView` calls it.
- [ ] `Inspector.close()` and `show(project:)` reset `diffMetrics`, with a test.
- [ ] One helper splits a camel-case kind into words; `ActivityEntry` and `ToolPresentation` both use it. The existing tests still pass.
- [ ] `MarkdownCache.blocks(id:text:final:)` has no default for `final`. Its throttle takes an injected clock (`any Clock<Duration>`, default `ContinuousClock()`), and the throttle test uses a test clock, not the wall clock.
- [ ] Footnote rewriting treats an escaped backtick (`` \` ``) as text, and leaves indented code blocks and fenced code inside block quotes unchanged. A test covers each.

tasks.subject: Task 9: The Settings window and the Muse Code pane
Task 10: Appearance: themes, text size and Reduce motion
tasks.description:
**Goal:** The Appearance pane saves the theme, text size, Reduce motion and Completion notifications, and the whole app draws in the chosen theme at the chosen reading size.

tasks.subject: Task 11: Completion notifications
tasks.description:
**Goal:** When a turn ends while mMac is not active and the preference is on, mMac posts Electron's notification, and clicking it opens that conversation.

**Files:**

- Create: `mac/mMac/Notifications.swift`
- Modify: `mac/mMac/AppController.swift`, `mac/mMac/MMacApp.swift`, `mac/mMac/AppearancePane.swift`

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- [ ] `Notifications.requestPermission()` asks `UNUserNotificationCenter` for alert and sound permission and returns the answer. When macOS refuses, the switch stays off and Settings shows "Notifications are off for mMac in System Settings." with "Open System Settings", which opens `x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.Notifications-Settings.extension`.
- [ ] `AppController` sets `workspace.turnFinished` for each Workspace. It posts when `CompletionNotice.shouldPost(previous:next:enabled:focused:)` is true, with `enabled` from the preferences and `focused` as `NSApp.isActive`. Electron checks the window's focus; `NSApp.isActive` is the Mac equivalent for a one-window app.
- [ ] The notification has `CompletionNotice.content(for:)`'s title and body, the sound `.default`, and `userInfo["sessionId"]`. Its identifier is the session id, so a second notice for one conversation replaces the first.
- [ ] Clicking it shows the main window, activates mMac and opens that conversation through `workspace.open(_:)`.
- [ ] mMac never asks for permission at launch, and the UI tests never see a permission prompt: no test turns notifications on.

**Verify:** `xcodebuild build -project mac/mMac.xcodeproj -scheme mMac -derivedDataPath .cache/mmac -quiet` succeeds; `CompletionNotice` is covered by Task 5's tests; Task 16 checks a real notification and its click.

tasks.description:

**Acceptance Criteria:**
